page.title: Best OBD GPS Tracker (2026): Spytec Pulse OBD vs Bouncie
page.desc: Bouncie suits one family car. For small fleets and yearly plans, the Spytec Pulse OBD is $8.95 a month with free hardware, 2-second updates and an unplug alert.
page.intro:
Short answer. For one family car, the best OBD GPS tracker is Bouncie: it adds crash alerts and car-health alerts, which Spytec does not advertise. For a business with several vehicles, or anyone who pays a year ahead, the best OBD GPS tracker is the Spytec Pulse OBD ({buy:spytec-pulse-obd}): free hardware, $8.95 a month on the annual plan ($107.40 a year), and 2-second updates while moving.

The top owner complaint about both brands is billing. In recent Trustpilot reviews, 14 of 41 mention billing or cancellation trouble. Spytec plans have no termination fee and a 30-day money-back guarantee. Get any cancellation confirmed in writing. Spytec also alerts you as soon as the tracker is unplugged, while Bouncie alerts you only when its device is plugged back in.

page.after:
What owners complain about

We read the latest Trustpilot reviews for both brands: 21 for Spytec and 20 for Bouncie. Poor support came up 16 times, billing or cancellation 14 times, and devices going offline 14 times. Accuracy or delays came up 8 times and app problems 7 times. Spytec's overall Trustpilot score is 2.9 out of 5 from 803 reviews. Bouncie's is 1.3 out of 5 from 939 reviews. Neither brand gets glowing reviews, so the cancel terms matter as much as the hardware.

The other common question is visibility. An OBD tracker sits in the port under the dash, where a driver can find it and pull it out. Bouncie says it can't send data without power, and its tamper alert arrives only when the device is reinstalled. Spytec says its software alerts you right away when the tracker is unplugged.

Which one by need

One family car or a teen driver: Bouncie, for its crash alerts and car-health alerts. Three or more work vehicles: the Spytec Pulse OBD ({buy:spytec-pulse-obd}). The hardware is free, the annual plan is $8.95 a month, and discounts apply automatically from 5 vehicles (5%) up to 100 or more (25%). A tracker the driver can't see: the Spytec Pulse Hardwired ({buy:spytec-pulse-hardwired}), at $12.95 a month on the annual plan. A trailer with no power: skip OBD and use a battery tracker such as Spytec's Atlas XL.

Not recommended

Don't choose Spytec's month-to-month plan if you'll keep the tracker a year. Twelve months at $14.95 is $179.40, against $107.40 on the annual plan. Don't count on any plug-in OBD tracker for theft recovery, because a thief can see it and unplug it. A hardwired unit is the better choice there. If a car will sit parked for weeks, unplug the OBD tracker to protect the car's battery.
